thread:
alex: quick sync — we need a concise decision on how to handle active/active routing when tenant residency = 'EU-only' but traffic spikes in APAC and EU region is degraded. proposals below, want alignment before i put an RFC follow-up.
marta: short answer: prefer soft-fail to nearest EU replica, not APAC. legal + compliance reasons.
raj: can we operationalize with a routing policy that prefers resident region unless we hit a latency SLO breach for N% of requests over T? then fallback to non-resident with strict logging.
jen: +1. need an audit trail and opt-in flag per tenant. otherwise customers will freak if data leaves boundary.
sam: can we do prefix-level routing? e.g., non-sensitive short prompts can route globally, PII/attachments stay EU-only.
alex: good call. but prefix classification adds latency and complexity. how many tenants actually need field-level residency? we have a tenant attribute table.
marta: most enterprise customers (>10 seats) flagged for EU residency do need full data residency. we can't split within a single request payload unless they opt-in and we vet.
raj: ops implications: if we block APAC fallback entirely, we risk user-visible errors during EU outage. tradeoff is SLA vs legal/contract. propose two-mode policy: "strict" and "lenient" per tenant.
jen: define modes:

* strict = never route outside resident region. return 503 or queued until recovery. log incident to customer and cs.
* lenient = route to closest region with encryption-in-transit & at-rest, annotate response with region header, strong audit.
sam: + add automatic degraded-experience notice in response metadata so apps can show messaging.
alex: ops automation sketch (pseudo-config):
```
routing_policy:
  tenant_flag: residency_mode # strict|lenient
  prefer_region: eu-west-1
  fallback_slo_threshold:
    error_rate_pct: 1
    latency_ms: 1200
    evaluation_window_s: 60
  fallback_behavior:
    lenient: route_to: nearest_region
    strict: block_with_requeue: true
```
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add metrics (resident-fallback-attempts, fallback-region, tenant-mode), add telemetry tag `residency_mode`, unit tests for routing decision tree.
marta: legal: any lenient fallback needs contractual opt-in and clear TOS. ping @legal for wording.
legal: confirmed — lenient must be explicit in contract or console toggle. also need a data-transfer CSV export per incident.
raj: fallback data handling: we must avoid writing persistent caches outside region for strict tenants. ephemeral KV allowed if TTL < 5m and encrypted with per-tenant key.
jen: quantization/caching note — if we serve a model variant from APAC for lenient tenant, make sure model fingerprinting and eval metrics match, otherwise quality regressions could slip.
alex: next steps I suggest: 1) add two-mode routing to RFC with decision matrix, 2) infra implement metrics and a feature-flag gated rollout, 3) legal + sales prepare contract template for lenient opt-in. I'll draft RFC and tag everyone.
marta: thanks — please include a short playbook for CS and oncall for when lenient fallback triggers. need clear customer comms.
sam: one more: mobile SDKs need a header so they can show a localized message if region changes. add to SDK roadmap.
alex: noted. will draft and circulate today. :thumbsup:
